passages.text: WSPR, "Weak Signal Propagation Reporter," is a protocol for low-power, digital communication on amateur radio frequencies. WSPR is designed to transmit and receive information efficiently over long distances, even under challenging radio propagation conditions.

WSPR encodes information in a series of tones and transmits it in short, controlled bursts using a highly efficient modulation scheme. The resulting signal is often too weak to hear but can be decoded by specialized software at a receiving station, which can extract the encoded information from the noise.

passages.text: WSPR (Weak Signal Propagation Reporter) is a protocol for low-power digital communication on amateur radio frequencies. Operators use it to study long-distance propagation, even under poor conditions.

paragraphs: Type3Single sends a callsign hash, a six-character Maidenhead locator, and reported power. The hash is not reversible; the receiver needs matching callsign context from another decoded message.
Type2Type3Paired alternates Type 2 (shown as F1/2) and Type 3 (shown as F2/2) messages, pairing a complex or long callsign with a long locator so the receiver can associate both.
